children: Nomura prefers Nippon AMC (NAM IN, 'Buy') within its coverage universe, followed by HDFC AMC (HDFCAMC IN, 'Buy'), as it expects Indian mutual funds' net equity inflows to rise sharply in August 2026.
"Within our coverage universe, we prefer Nippon AMC for its consistent AUM market share gains, followed by HDFC AMC," Nomura said in its latest note on Friday.

The brokerage expects August net equity inflows, excluding arbitrage, at Rs 410 billion, up around 36% month-on-month from Rs 301 billion in July. Excluding new fund offers (NFOs), flows are estimated at Rs 345 billion, implying a 15% month-on-month increase.

For Nippon AMC, Nomura expects the flow share at 8.3% in August, with its three-month average flow share 2.1 percentage points above its AUM share of 7.4%. "NAM strong" is among the key takeaways from the brokerage's August flow preview.

HDFC AMC's flow share is expected at 7.0% in August, down from 9.1% in July and below its AUM share of 12.7%. Nomura said the lower flow share was "due to outflows in BAF, Aggressive Hybrid funds in Aug-26F". Its three-month average flow share remains 4.4 percentage points below its AUM share.

ICICI AMC's (ICICIAMC IN, Not rated) flow share is expected to "inch up m-m to 7.4%" but remains well below its AUM share of 13.8%. Its three-month average flow share is 4.4 percentage points below its AUM share.

SBI AMC (SBIFUNDS IN, Not rated), meanwhile, is expected to see its flow share "moderate sharply m-m to 4.3%" from 9.7% in July. Nomura's assessment for August is therefore "NAM strong; SBIFM weak; HDFCAMC lower, ICICIAMC higher m-m".

ABSL AMC's (ABSLAMC IN, Not rated) equity flow share is expected to improve to 1.5% in August from 0.4% in July, driven by flows into flexi-cap, balanced advantage and multi-asset allocation funds. Bandhan AMC, which is unlisted, had the highest ex-NFO flow share at 9.4%.

At the industry level, Nomura expects small-cap funds to be the largest contributor to August equity inflows at Rs 88 billion, accounting for a 26% share. Mid-cap funds are expected to attract Rs 66 billion, or 19%, while flexi-cap funds could see Rs 52 billion, or 15%.

"Small and mid-cap domination continues; large-cap still negative," Nomura said. The brokerage expects large-cap funds to see an outflow of Rs 10 billion, or a -3% share, compared with an outflow of Rs 13 billion in July.
Multi-cap flows are expected to improve month-on-month to Rs 37 billion, accounting for an 11% share, while large-and-mid-cap flows are expected to remain largely stable at Rs 35 billion, or 10%.

Within hybrid funds, Nomura expects aggressive hybrid schemes to garner Rs 59 billion, including Rs 14 billion excluding NFOs, while multi-asset allocation is expected to attract Rs 37 billion. The balanced advantage category is expected to remain weak, with an outflow of Rs 5 billion versus an outflow of Rs 3 billion in July.

"ELSS outflow continues; sectoral/thematic flows strong," Nomura said. The brokerage expects strong sectoral and thematic inflows of Rs 25 billion in August, compared with Rs 13 billion in July, while ELSS flows remain negative amid the government's push for the new tax regime and the three-year lock-in requirement.

Nomura expects two potentially large NFOs in August - Bandhan Contra Fund, estimated at Rs 20 billion, and SBI Balanced Hybrid Fund, estimated at Rs 45 billion. These would take the FY27 year-to-date monthly average to Rs 365 billion, compared with the FY26 average monthly flow of Rs 379 billion.
"Net Flow Navigator is our monthly estimate of net equity inflows into Indian mutual funds, providing a timely, ground-up read on domestic equity appetite," Nomura said.

title: Nippon AMC, HDFC AMC preferred by Nomura as mutual fund equity inflows seen rising 36% in August
